literal: Shizu, Emperor Taiwu — taboo name Tao — was Taizong Emperor Mingyuan's eldest son. His mother was Lady Du, Honored Consort.
idiomatic: Shizu, Emperor Taiwu, bore the taboo name Tao. He was the eldest son of Taizong, Emperor Mingyuan; his mother was Lady Du, Honored Consort.

literal: In the fifth year of Tianci he was born in the Eastern Palace. His form and bearing were extraordinary; Taizu marveled and was pleased, saying: "He who will complete my enterprise must be this boy."
idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianci he was born in the Eastern Palace. His bearing was strikingly unusual; Taizu wondered at him and said, "The one who will finish what I began is this child."

literal: " In the seventh year of Taichang, fourth month, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Taiping; fifth month, he became regent of the realm.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of the seventh year of Taichang he was made Prince of Taiping; in the fifth month he was appointed regent.

literal: Taizong fell ill and ordered the Emperor to oversee all government affairs. He was intelligent and magnanimous, his mind open and at ease.
idiomatic: When Taizong fell ill, he put the heir in charge of government. The prince was bright and broad-minded, untroubled in spirit.

literal: Eighth year, eleventh month, day renshen, [1] he ascended the imperial throne and proclaimed a general amnesty throughout the realm.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the eighth year, on the renshen day, [1] he took the throne and granted amnesty to the empire.

literal: Twelfth month: his late mother was posthumously honored as Empress Mi; Chancellor of State Changsun Song was advanced to Prince of Beiping, Minister of Works Xi Jin to Prince of Yicheng, Duke of Lantian Changsun Han to Prince of Pingyang; the rest received general advancement of noble rank, each according to merit.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month he raised his late mother to Empress Mi; Changsun Song, Chancellor of State, became Prince of Beiping; Xi Jin, Minister of Works, Prince of Yicheng; Changsun Han, Duke of Lantian, Prince of Pingyang; and the rest were promoted in rank, each as deserved.

literal: Thereupon prohibitions were lifted, grudges released, granaries opened, and the destitute relieved; very many displaced people south of the Yellow River came in groups to submit.
idiomatic: He ended arbitrary detention, cleared old grievances, opened the storehouses, and aided the poor; refugees south of the Yellow River flocked inward in great numbers.

literal: Shiguang year 1, spring, first month, day bingyin: Prince of Anding Mi died.
idiomatic: In the first year of Shiguang, on the bingyin day of the first month of spring, Prince of Anding Mi died.

literal: Summer, fourth month, day jiachen: the court toured east and visited Daning.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on the jiachen day, the emperor toured east to Daning.

literal: Autumn, seventh month: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn the court returned to the capital.

literal: Eighth month: the Rouran led sixty thousand horsemen into Yunzhong, killing and plundering officials and people, and captured Shengle Palace.
idiomatic: In the eighth month the Rouran brought sixty thousand horsemen into Yunzhong, slaughtered and looted the people, and took Shengle Palace.

literal: Ziyangzi Wei Puwen led light cavalry against them; the barbarians then withdrew.
idiomatic: Wei Puwen, Lord of Ziyang, led light horse against them and the enemy withdrew.

literal: An edict ordered Prince of Pingyang Changsun Han and others to strike a Rouran sub-chief; they defeated him, killed several thousand, and captured more than ten thousand horses.
idiomatic: The emperor ordered Changsun Han, Prince of Pingyang, and others to attack a Rouran sub-chief; they broke him, killed several thousand men, and took more than ten thousand horses.

literal: The account is in the Rouran treatise.
idiomatic: The full account is given in the treatise on the Rouran.

literal: Ninth month: a great muster of chariots and foot soldiers; troops were drilled at the eastern suburb and the armies were divided—fifty thousand horsemen—to campaign north.
idiomatic: In the ninth month he mustered chariots and infantry, drilled the army at the eastern suburb, and arrayed fifty thousand horsemen for a northern expedition.

literal: Winter, twelfth month: Prince of Pingyang Changsun Han and others were sent to campaign against the Rouran.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month of winter he sent Changsun Han, Prince of Pingyang, and others against the Rouran.

literal: The imperial carriage halted at Zuoshan; the Rouran fled north and the armies pursued, taking great booty before returning.
idiomatic: The emperor halted at Zuoshan; the Rouran fled north, the armies pursued, won a great haul, and returned.

literal: That year Liu Yifu was deposed and killed by his ministers Xu Xianzhi and others; his younger brother Yilong was installed.
idiomatic: That year Liu Yifu was overthrown and killed by his ministers Xu Xianzhi and others, who set up his younger brother Yilong.

literal: Year 2, spring, first month, day jimao: the imperial carriage returned from the northern campaign and distributed captured livestock to the officers and soldiers, each according to merit.
idiomatic: In the second year, on the jimao day of the first month of spring, the court returned from the northern expedition and divided the captured herds among officers and men, each as earned.

literal: Second month: Murong Kesilin rebelled at Beiping, broke the commandery seat; the governor and defending generals attacked and defeated him.
idiomatic: In the second month Murong Kesilin rebelled in Beiping and stormed the commandery seat; the governor and garrison commanders defeated him.

literal: Third month, day bingchen: the wet-nurse Lady Dou was honored as Dowager Protector.
idiomatic: On the bingchen day of the third month the wet-nurse Lady Dou was honored as Dowager Protector.

literal: Day dingsi: Prince of Beiping Changsun Song was made Grand Commandant, Prince of Pingyang Changsun Han Chancellor of State, Prince of Yicheng Xi Jin Minister of Works.
idiomatic: On the dingsi day Changsun Song, Prince of Beiping, became Grand Commandant; Changsun Han, Prince of Pingyang, Chancellor of State; and Xi Jin, Prince of Yicheng, Minister of Works.

literal: Day gengshen: the former Eastern Palace was converted into Wanshou Palace; the Yong'an and Anle halls were raised, the Linwang Observatory and Jiuhua Hall.
idiomatic: On the gengshen day the old Eastern Palace was made Wanshou Palace; the Yong'an and Anle halls were built, with the Linwang Observatory and Jiuhua Hall.

literal: More than a thousand new characters were first devised. An edict said: "In former times Emperor Xuan of the Yellow lineage created and fashioned things; he ordered Cang Jie to establish writing from the traces of birds and beasts.
idiomatic: More than a thousand new characters were devised for the first time. An edict declared: "Long ago the Yellow Emperor fashioned the world and ordered Cang Jie to fix writing from the tracks of birds and beasts."

literal: From that time onward scripts were altered with the age; thus seal, clerical, cursive, and regular forms have all circulated in the world.
idiomatic: "Since then each age has changed the script, so seal, clerical, cursive, and regular forms have all been in use."

literal: Yet because long transmission has lost the true forms, the written style is confused and the meeting of meanings unsatisfactory—not how to show a standard to later ages.
idiomatic: "But long transmission has blurred the true forms, so texts are corrupt and meanings fail to meet—this is no way to set a standard for posterity."

literal: Confucius said: when names are not correct, affairs do not succeed—this is what he meant.
idiomatic: "Confucius said that when names are not correct, affairs do not succeed. He spoke of this."

literal: Now writing is fixed for what the age uses; it is to be promulgated far and near and made the permanent model."
idiomatic: "Now we fix the characters the age shall use, promulgate them far and near, and make them the lasting model forever."

literal: Summer, fourth month: an edict that General of Dragon Celerity Bu Dui and Master of Ceremonies Hu Gu were to go as envoys to Liu Yilong.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer he ordered Bu Dui, General of Dragon Celerity, and Hu Gu, Master of Ceremonies, as envoys to Liu Yilong.

literal: Fifth month: an edict that throughout the realm every ten households were to furnish one large ox to haul grain to the frontier.
idiomatic: In the fifth month he decreed that every ten households in the empire must supply one large ox to haul grain to the border.

literal: Autumn, ninth month: the Yong'an and Anle halls were completed; day dingmao, a great feast marked their completion.
idiomatic: In the ninth month of autumn the Yong'an and Anle halls were finished; on the dingmao day a great feast celebrated them.

literal: Winter, tenth month: troops were drilled at the western suburb.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter the army was drilled at the western suburb.

literal: Day guimao: the imperial carriage campaigned north; Prince of Pingyang Changsun Han and others crossed the desert in pursuit and the Rouran fled north.
idiomatic: On the guimao day the emperor marched north; Changsun Han, Prince of Pingyang, and others crossed the desert in pursuit and the Rouran fled north.

literal: The matter is fully set forth in the Rouran treatise.
idiomatic: The full account is in the treatise on the Rouran.

literal: That year Helian Ququ died; his son Chang presumptuously succeeded.
idiomatic: That year Helian Ququ died and his son Chang seized the throne.

literal: Year 3, spring, first month, day renshen: the imperial carriage returned from the northern campaign.
idiomatic: In the third year, on the renshen day of the first month of spring, the court returned from the northern expedition.

literal: Captured goods were distributed to the officers and soldiers; those who marched and those who remained each received according to merit.
idiomatic: Booty was divided among the troops; those who had marched and those who had stayed behind were rewarded each as earned.

literal: Qifu Chipo sent envoys with tribute and requested permission to campaign against Helian Chang.
idiomatic: Qifu Chipo sent tribute and asked leave to attack Helian Chang.

literal: Second month: the Imperial Academy was founded east of the city; Confucius was sacrificed to, with Yan Yuan as associate.
idiomatic: In the second month the Imperial Academy was founded east of the city; Confucius was honored and Yan Yuan paired with him.

literal: Summer, fifth month, day xinmao: Duke of Zhongshan Yuan Zuan was advanced to prince; Duke of Nan'an Yuan Su had his former title Prince of Changshan restored.
idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer, on the xinmao day, Yuan Zuan, Duke of Zhongshan, was raised to princely rank; Yuan Su, Duke of Nan'an, had his former title Prince of Changshan restored.

literal: Sixth month: the court visited the old palace at Yunzhong and paid respects at the imperial tombs;
idiomatic: In the sixth month the emperor visited the old palace at Yunzhong and the ancestral tombs;

literal: west to Wuyuan, hunting on Yinshan;
idiomatic: west to Wuyuan, hunting on Yinshan;

literal: east to Hedou Mountain.
idiomatic: east to Hedou Mountain.

literal: Autumn, seventh month: a horse-shooting platform was built on Changchuan; the Emperor personally mounted the platform to watch the running horses;
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn a horse-shooting terrace was built on Changchuan; the emperor mounted it to watch the races;

literal: princes, dukes, and the chieftains of the various states galloped and shot; those who hit the mark received gold, brocade, and silk floss, each according to merit.
idiomatic: princes, dukes, and foreign chieftains rode and shot; hits were rewarded with gold, brocade, and silk, each as earned.

literal: Eighth month: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: In the eighth month the court returned to the capital.

literal: Liu Yilong sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: Liu Yilong sent envoys with tribute.

literal: The Emperor, because Ququ was dead and his sons were attacking one another, in the ninth month sent Minister of Works Xi Jin with General of Righteous Troops Feng Li and Yanzhou Inspector Yan Pu to strike Puban, and Song general Zhou Ji with Luozhou Inspector Yu Liben to strike Shancheng.
idiomatic: Because Ququ was dead and his sons were at war, in the ninth month the emperor sent Xi Jin, Minister of Works, with Feng Li, General of Righteous Troops, and Yan Pu, governor of Yanzhou, against Puban, and Zhou Ji of Song with Yu Liben, governor of Luozhou, against Shancheng.

literal: Winter, tenth month, day dingsi: the imperial carriage campaigned west, visited Yunzhong, and came to Junzi Ford.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on the dingsi day, the emperor marched west, came to Yunzhong, and halted at Junzi Ford.

literal: Heaven suddenly turned bitter cold; within days the river froze solid.
idiomatic: A sudden bitter cold fell; within days the river was ice.

literal: Eleventh month, day wuyin: the Emperor led twenty thousand light horse in a surprise attack on Helian Chang; day renchen, he reached below the city walls and moved more than ten thousand households back.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the wuyin day, the emperor led twenty thousand light cavalry in a surprise raid on Helian Chang; on the renchen day he reached the walls and carried off more than ten thousand households.

literal: The account is in the Chang treatise.
idiomatic: The account is given in the treatise on Chang.

literal: At Zuoshan the captives were distributed to the officers and soldiers, each according to merit.
idiomatic: At Zuoshan the captives were divided among the troops, each as earned.

literal: Xi Jin had not yet reached Puban when Chang's defending general Helian Yisheng abandoned the city and fled west.
idiomatic: Before Xi Jin reached Puban, Chang's defender Helian Yisheng abandoned the city and fled west.

literal: [2] Chang's younger brother Zhuxing held Chang'an; Yisheng joined Zhuxing and they fled west from Chang'an toward Anding.
idiomatic: [2] Chang's brother Zhuxing held Chang'an; Yisheng joined him and they fled west from Chang'an toward Anding.

literal: Xi Jin then entered Puban.
idiomatic: Xi Jin then entered Puban.

literal: Twelfth month: an edict that Xi Jin was to press west and hold Chang'an.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month he ordered Xi Jin to advance west and secure Chang'an.

literal: The Di and Qiang of Qin and Yong all rebelled against Chang and came to Xi Jin to surrender.
idiomatic: The Di and Qiang of Qin and Yong all turned from Chang and surrendered to Xi Jin.

literal: Yang Xuan, Di king of Wudu, and Juqu Mengxun and others all sent envoys to submit inward.
idiomatic: Yang Xuan, Di king of Wudu, Juqu Mengxun, and others all sent envoys to submit.

literal: Year 4, spring, first month, day yiyou: the imperial carriage returned from the western campaign and bestowed on the civil and military officials who remained at the capital captives, silk, horses, and oxen, each according to merit.
idiomatic: In the fourth year, on the yiyou day of the first month of spring, the court returned from the western expedition and rewarded the officials who had stayed at the capital with captives, silk, horses, and oxen, each as earned.

literal: Very many of those who followed the march died on the road; barely sixteen or seventeen in ten reached the capital.
idiomatic: Many who had marched died on the road; scarcely one in six reached the capital.

literal: Day jihai: the court traveled to Youzhou.
idiomatic: On the jihai day the emperor went to Youzhou.

literal: Helian Chang sent his younger brother Duke of Pingyuan Ding with twenty thousand men toward Chang'an.
idiomatic: Helian Chang sent his brother Ding, Duke of Pingyuan, with twenty thousand men toward Chang'an.

literal: When the Emperor heard, he sent men to Yinshan to fell timber and build siege engines on a great scale.
idiomatic: Hearing this, the emperor sent men to Yinshan to fell timber and build siege engines in great numbers.

literal: Second month: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: In the second month the court returned to the capital.

literal: Third month, day bingzi: Prince of Gaoliang Li was sent to garrison Chang'an.
idiomatic: On the bingzi day of the third month Prince of Gaoliang Li was sent to garrison Chang'an.

literal: An edict that Bearer of the Golden Mace Huan Dai was to build a bridge at Junzi Ford.
idiomatic: He ordered Huan Dai, Bearer of the Golden Mace, to build a bridge at Junzi Ford.

literal: Day dingchou: Prince of Guangping Lian died.
idiomatic: On the dingchou day Prince of Guangping Lian died.

literal: Summer, fourth month, day dingwei: an edict that Supernumerary Palace Attendant Bu Dui, Master of Ceremonies Hu Gu, and others were to go as envoys to Liu Yilong.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on the dingwei day, he ordered Bu Dui, Supernumerary Palace Attendant, Hu Gu, Master of Ceremonies, and others as envoys to Liu Yilong.

literal: That month troops were drilled and martial arts rehearsed; the armies were divided—Chancellor Changsun Han, Court Director Changsun Daosheng, and Director of Imperial Clan E Qing, thirty thousand horsemen as vanguard; Prince of Changshan Su, Grand Steward Bing Dui, and General Yuan Taipi, thirty thousand foot as rear guard; Prince of Nanyang Fuzhen, Bearer of the Golden Mace Huan Dai, and General Yao Huangmei, thirty thousand foot to manage siege engines; General He Duoluo, three thousand picked horse as scouts.
idiomatic: That month the army was drilled: Changsun Han, Chancellor, Changsun Daosheng, Court Director, and E Qing, Director of the Imperial Clan, led thirty thousand horse as vanguard; Prince of Changshan Su, Grand Steward Bing Dui, and General Yuan Taipi, thirty thousand foot as rear; Prince of Nanyang Fuzhen, Huan Dai, Bearer of the Golden Mace, and General Yao Huangmei, thirty thousand foot with siege train; General He Duoluo, three thousand elite horse as scouts.

literal: Fifth month: the imperial carriage campaigned west against Helian Chang.
idiomatic: In the fifth month the emperor marched west against Helian Chang.

literal: Day xinsi: he crossed Junzi Ford.
idiomatic: On the xinsi day he crossed Junzi Ford.

literal: The Hu chieftain Quezi of Sancheng led his people inward in submission.
idiomatic: Quezi, Hu chieftain of Sancheng, led his people to submit.

literal: The Emperor halted at Balin Mountain, built a fort, left the baggage train, and with thirty thousand light horse went ahead.
idiomatic: The emperor halted at Balin Mountain, built a camp, left the baggage, and pressed on with thirty thousand light horse.

literal: Day wuxu: he reached the Black Water; the Emperor personally prayed to Heaven and reported to the spirits of the ancestors, swearing the host.
idiomatic: On the wuxu day he reached the Black Water; the emperor prayed to Heaven and invoked the ancestral spirits before the army.

literal: Sixth month, day jiachen: Chang led his host out of the city and was utterly defeated.
idiomatic: On the jiachen day of the sixth month Chang led his army out and was utterly broken.

literal: The matter is in the Chang treatise.
idiomatic: The account is in the treatise on Chang.

literal: Chang with several hundred horsemen under his command fled southwest to Shanggui; the armies pursued in victory to below the city walls; more than ten thousand were killed in battle; on the field Chang's younger brother Duke of Henan Man and his brother's son Mengxun were slain.
idiomatic: Chang fled southwest to Shanggui with a few hundred horse; the armies pursued to the walls and killed more than ten thousand; in the fighting Chang's brother Man, Duke of Henan, and his nephew Mengxun were slain.

literal: At dusk Chang's Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wen Zhiba seized the city; that night he took Chang's mother and fled.
idiomatic: At dusk Wen Zhiba, Chang's Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, held the city; that night he fled with Chang's mother.

literal: Day yisi: the imperial carriage entered the city; Chang's younger brothers and all their mothers, sisters, wives, concubines, and palace women—tens of thousands; the treasuries' gems, chariots, banners, and utensils beyond counting; Chang's Masters of Writing Wang Mai, Xue Chao, and others were captured, with Mao Xiuzhi, general to Sima Dezong, and several thousand men of Qin and Yong; more than three hundred thousand horses and tens of millions of cattle and sheep.
idiomatic: On the yisi day the emperor entered the city. He took Chang's brothers, their mothers, sisters, wives, concubines, and palace women by the tens of thousands; treasure, chariots, banners, and goods beyond count; Chang's Masters of Writing Wang Mai and Xue Chao; Mao Xiuzhi, general to Sima Dezong; and several thousand men of Qin and Yong; more than three hundred thousand horses and tens of millions of cattle and sheep.

literal: Chang's palace women, captives, gold and silver, rare objects, silk, and cloth were distributed to the officers and soldiers, each according to merit.
idiomatic: Chang's palace women, captives, gold, silver, treasures, and cloth were divided among the troops, each as earned.

literal: Chang's younger brother Duke of Pingyuan Ding resisted Minister of Works Xi Jin at Chang'an; E Qing with five thousand horse campaigned against him; he fled west to Shanggui.
idiomatic: Chang's brother Ding, Duke of Pingyuan, held Chang'an against Xi Jin; E Qing with five thousand horse drove him west to Shanggui.

literal: Day xinyou: the army withdrew; Prince of Changshan Su and Bearer of the Golden Mace Huan Dai were left to garrison Tongwan.
idiomatic: On the xinyou day the army withdrew; Prince of Changshan Su and Huan Dai, Bearer of the Golden Mace, were left to garrison Tongwan.

literal: Autumn, seventh month, day jimao: a platform was built on Zuoling; horses were raced and archery practiced; those who hit the mark received gold, brocade, and silk floss, each according to merit.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on the jimao day, a terrace was raised on Zuoling for racing and archery; hits were rewarded with gold, brocade, and silk, each as earned.

literal: The Rouran raided Yunzhong; hearing that Helian Chang was broken, they feared and withdrew.
idiomatic: The Rouran raided Yunzhong; hearing of Chang's defeat, they fled in fear.

literal: Eighth month, day renzi: the imperial carriage returned from the western campaign; a feast celebrated merit and report was made at the ancestral temple; captured goods were distributed to the officials who had remained at the capital, each according to merit.
idiomatic: On the renzi day of the eighth month the court returned from the west; a feast honored the victors and the ancestral temple was told; booty was divided among the capital officials, each as earned.

literal: Ninth month, day dingyou: the people of Anding raised the city in surrender.
idiomatic: On the dingyou day of the ninth month the people of Anding surrendered the city.

literal: Winter, eleventh month: Di king Yang Xuan was made Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Jing, Liang, Yi, and Ning provinces, Acting General Who Conquers the South, Inspector of Liangzhou, and King of Southern Qin.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter Yang Xuan, Di king, was made commander of all armies in Jing, Liang, Yi, and Ning, acting General Who Conquers the South, inspector of Liangzhou, and King of Southern Qin.

literal: Twelfth month: the court traveled to Zhongshan; more than ten district magistrates were dismissed for corruption.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month the emperor went to Zhongshan; more than ten magistrates were removed for graft.

literal: Day guimao: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: On the guimao day the court returned to the capital.

literal: Half the field tax along the route was remitted.
idiomatic: Half the land tax along the route was remitted.

literal: Shenju year 1, spring, first month: because prefects and magistrates throughout the realm often acted unlawfully, the loyal and able were carefully selected to replace them all.
idiomatic: In the first year of Shenju, first month of spring, because magistrates throughout the empire often broke the law, trustworthy men were chosen to replace them.

literal: Day xinwei: Prince of Jingzhao Li died.
idiomatic: On the xinwei day Prince of Jingzhao Li died.

literal: Second month: the era name was changed.
idiomatic: In the second month the reign title was changed.

literal: Helian Chang withdrew and encamped at Pingliang.
idiomatic: Helian Chang withdrew to Pingliang.

literal: Minister of Works Xi Jin advanced on Anding; General Qiu Dui was defeated by Chang; Supervising Censor An Gu went out to battle and captured Chang.
idiomatic: Xi Jin, Minister of Works, advanced on Anding; General Qiu Dui was beaten by Chang; Supervising Censor An Gu took the field and captured Chang.

literal: Chang's remaining host installed Chang's younger brother Ding as king and fled back to Pingliang.
idiomatic: Chang's remnant forces made his brother Ding king and fled back to Pingliang.

literal: Third month, day guiyou: an edict that Palace Attendant Gu Bi was to welcome Helian Chang.
idiomatic: On the guiyou day of the third month he ordered Palace Attendant Gu Bi to escort Helian Chang.

literal: Day xinsi: Bi and others brought Chang to the capital.
idiomatic: On the xinsi day Bi brought Chang to the capital.

literal: Minister of Works Xi Jin pursued Ding to Mama Ridge at Pingliang and was captured by Ding.
idiomatic: Xi Jin pursued Ding to Mama Ridge near Pingliang and was taken by Ding.
